_comment: Tier 2 edge defense: Cloudflare Rate Limiting Rules for zone clariora.com.au.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: wrangler.toml sets run_worker_first = true, so today EVERY
request to the zone - including static assets and hostile floods - boots the
Worker and is billed as an invocation before any of our own limiter code runs.
Rules in the http_ratelimit phase execute in Cloudflare's edge proxy BEFORE the
Worker is dispatched, so a blocked request costs zero Worker invocations, zero D1
reads and zero Durable Object wakeups. This is the only layer in the stack that
can actually drop traffic before compute.
DEPLOY: infra/cloudflare/deploy-rate-limits.mjs (PUTs this as the zone entrypoint
ruleset). Rules are evaluated top to bottom and evaluation stops at the first rule
that blocks, so the specific high-cost rules MUST stay above the catch-all.
- characteristics must include cf.colo.id on Free/Pro/Business plans; counting is
then per-datacentre, so effective global limits are somewhat higher than stated.
- Enterprise can add http.request.headers["authorization"] as a characteristic to
count per-token instead of per-IP. Until then, per-UID enforcement is Tier 3's
job and this layer is deliberately IP-only.
name: clariora-edge-rate-limits
description: Volumetric IP rate limiting in front of the Clariora Worker and Firebase endpoints

rules.description: Telegram Bot API webhook - generous ceiling, never starve payment callbacks
rules._rationale: Telegram retries failed webhook deliveries. Dropping a successful_payment callback loses a real Stars purchase, so this ceiling exists only to stop a spoofed flood, not to shape normal traffic. The HMAC secret check in the Worker is the real authenticity gate.

rules.description: LLM inference - highest marginal cost per request in the product
rules._rationale: Every request past this point can spend Groq / NVIDIA / OpenRouter tokens. 10/min/IP is far above any human study session and far below anything worth scripting. Longer mitigation timeout because the cost of a false negative here is money, not latency.

rules.description: Authentication and session endpoints - credential stuffing surface
rules._rationale: Unauthenticated entry points. /api/v1/auth/telegram in particular runs an HMAC verification and a D1 upsert per call with no caller identity to meter against, so IP is the only key available at this layer.

rules.description: Billing and payment verification - external API spend and grant writes
rules._rationale: TON verification calls the paid TonCenter API; Stars invoice creation calls the Telegram Bot API. Both are third-party spend triggered by an unauthenticated-ish request shape.

rules.description: Bulk question bank and shards - scraping target, large egress
rules._rationale: These paths return the paid asset itself (exam_data.json is ~2MB). A scraper walking them is both an egress bill and the theft of the product. Legitimate clients fetch each of these at most a handful of times per session.

rules.description: State sync and telemetry writes - D1 write amplification
rules._rationale: Each of these is a D1 write. A client stuck in a re-render loop can emit these continuously; the Worker-side limiter catches that too, but only after paying for the invocation.
The spec'd standard-endpoint ceiling. Sits last so the cheaper specific rules above always win.

rules.description: Burst guard - absorbs the first second of a flood before the 60s windows react
rules._rationale: A 60-second window lets an attacker deliver 100 requests in 100 milliseconds and then idle. The short window caps instantaneous concurrency, which is what actually drives Worker and D1 cost spikes.
